purposes.src/didact/createElement.js: What JSX compiles to: a plain `{ type, props }` object with the children inside `props`. Every other file in the library passes these around.
purposes.src/didact/dom.js: The two places the library touches a real DOM node: making one from an element, and bringing its properties and listeners in line with new props.
purposes.src/didact/renderSync.js: The first draft of `render`: walk the tree recursively and append nodes as you go. Assignment 4 replaces it with a work loop; the file stays so you can compare.
purposes.src/didact/state.js: The library's shared bookkeeping (what to work on next, the tree under construction) in one object, because an ES module can't share a variable that other modules reassign.
purposes.src/didact/render.js: `render` and the work loop: units of work that the browser can interrupt, one fiber at a time.
purposes.src/didact/reconcile.js: Decides which fibers a parent's children become. It starts by making a fresh fiber for every child and grows into the comparison with the previous render.
purposes.src/didact/index.js: The `Didact` object an app imports: `createElement` and `render`, then the hooks as they arrive.
purposes.src/didact/commit.js: Applies a finished fiber tree to the DOM in one pass, so nobody sees half a render.
purposes.src/didact/hooks.js: `useState` and `useEffect`: state and effects that belong to a component and survive its re-renders, kept on the fiber.
purposes.src/app/TodoApp.js: The todo list, written the way an application would write it, on top of your Didact.
purposes.src/main.js: The finished program: mounts the todo app into the page's `#root`.

book.title: Build React yourself

sources.title: Creating Our Own React From Scratch
sources.author: Wim Jongeneel

book.author: Rodrigo Pombo
book.headline: Learn what React does by writing it
book.lede: Rebuild React's core in JavaScript, one assignment at a time: elements, a work loop over fibers, the commit phase, reconciliation by position and by key, function components, useState, useEffect, and a todo app that runs on your own library. Your code runs on a small DOM, and the checker compares what it draws with real React 19.3.1 on jsdom. Where the two posts this follows disagree with React as it is today, the tests follow React.
book.credits: Expected outputs come from React 19.3.1 running on jsdom 30.1.3, plus small independent models for counts of work. The book keeps your progress in this browser only.

jobs.assignments/assignment_01_create_element: Hand the scenario file to `runScenarioFile` from the harness, together with your `createElement`; it builds each element the scenario lists and prints it.
jobs.src/didact/createElement.js: Write `createElement(type, props, ...children)` and `createTextElement(text)`. An element is `{ type, props }` with every child inside `props.children`, and a string or number child becomes a text element.

jobs.assignments/assignment_02_dom_props.js: Pass your `createDom` and `updateDom` to `runScenarioFile`; the scenario creates one node, updates it a few times and clicks it.
jobs.src/didact/dom.js: Write `createDom` and `updateDom(dom, prevProps, nextProps)`. `createDom` makes the node for an element. `updateDom` writes only what changed: new and changed properties, removed ones cleared, and a listener swapped when its handler changed.

jobs.assignments/assignment_03_first_render.j: Pass your `render` from `renderSync.js` to `runScenarioFile`; the scenario renders a tree and dumps the container.
jobs.src/didact/renderSync.js: Write `render(element, container)`: create the DOM for the element, do the same for its children, and append everything to the container.

jobs.assignments/assignment_04_fibers.js: Pass your `Didact` object to `runScenarioFile`; the scenario renders a tree, runs idle periods of a size it picks, and dumps the container.
jobs.src/didact/state.js: Create the shared state object, holding the next unit of work and the root of the tree being built.
jobs.src/didact/render.js: Write `render`, `workLoop` and `performUnitOfWork`. `render` only schedules the work. Each idle period runs fibers until `timeRemaining()` falls below 1, one fiber per unit of work.
jobs.src/didact/reconcile.js: Write `reconcileChildren(wipFiber, elements)`: give every element a fiber of its own and link the fibers with `child`, `sibling` and `parent`.

jobs.assignments/assignment_05_commit.js: Pass your `Didact` object to `runScenarioFile`; the scenario now dumps the container between idle periods.
jobs.src/didact/commit.js: Write `commitRoot` and `commitWork`: once the last unit is done, append the finished tree to the container in a single pass.
jobs.src/didact/render.js: Stop attaching DOM nodes while units run. Keep the tree under construction as `wipRoot`, and call `commitRoot` after the last unit.

jobs.assignments/assignment_06_reconcile.js: Pass your `Didact` object to `runScenarioFile`; the scenario renders a second tree into the container that already holds the first.
jobs.src/didact/state.js: Add `currentRoot`, the last tree you committed, and `deletions`, the fibers to remove.
jobs.src/didact/render.js: Point the new root's `alternate` at `currentRoot`, the tree you committed last time, and reset `deletions` on every `render`.
jobs.src/didact/reconcile.js: Rewrite `reconcileChildren` to compare each element with the old fiber at the same position. Same type reuses the old DOM node and updates it, a different type gets a new node, and an old fiber with no element left is queued for deletion.
jobs.src/didact/commit.js: Act on what reconciliation decided: put a new node before the next sibling that already has a DOM node, so it keeps its position, call `updateDom` for an update, and remove each deleted node exactly once.

jobs.assignments/assignment_07_keys.js: Pass your `Didact` object to `runScenarioFile`; the scenario re-renders lists whose children carry keys.
jobs.src/didact/reconcile.js: Match a child to the old child with the same `key`, wherever the old one stood, as long as the keys that both lists share keep their order. Children without a key still match by position.

jobs.assignments/assignment_08_reorder.js: Pass your `Didact` object to `runScenarioFile`; the scenario shuffles keyed lists.
jobs.src/didact/reconcile.js: Let a key match its old child even when the order of the shared keys changed.
jobs.src/didact/commit.js: Move the existing DOM node of a reordered child instead of recreating it, so it keeps its state.

jobs.assignments/assignment_09_function_compo: Pass your `Didact` object to `runScenarioFile`; the scenario renders trees that contain the catalog's function components.
jobs.src/didact/render.js: Branch in `performUnitOfWork`: a fiber whose type is a function has no DOM node, and its children are whatever calling the function returns.
jobs.src/didact/commit.js: Find the parent DOM node by walking up through fibers that have none, and the node to remove by walking down through them.

jobs.assignments/assignment_10_use_state.js: Pass your `Didact` object to `runScenarioFile`; the scenario clicks buttons in catalog components and dumps the result.
jobs.src/didact/hooks.js: Write `useState(initial)`: state kept on the fiber, found again on the next render by hook index. The setter takes an updater function, queues it, and schedules a new render from the root.
jobs.src/didact/render.js: Before you call a function component, set `wipFiber`, give it an empty `hooks` array and reset `hookIndex`.

jobs.assignments/assignment_11_use_effect.js: Pass your `Didact` object to `runScenarioFile`; the scenario mounts, updates and removes catalog components that log from their effects.
jobs.src/didact/hooks.js: Write `useEffect(effect, deps)`: remember the effect and its dependencies on the fiber, and keep whatever cleanup function the effect returned.
jobs.src/didact/commit.js: After the DOM is updated, run the cleanups of effects that run again, then the effects that are new or whose dependencies changed. Run a removed component's cleanups too.

jobs.assignments/assignment_12_todo_app.js: Pass your `Didact` object and your `TodoApp` to `runScenarioFile`; the scenario types into the form, adds items, toggles and removes them.
jobs.src/app/TodoApp.js: Write `TodoApp` with function components on your Didact: a form with a controlled input, a list of keyed items, and a toggle and a remove button on each item.
jobs.src/main.js: Mount `TodoApp` into the page's `#root`, so `index.html` shows a working app.

requires: react, react-dom and jsdom, only for fresh test sets (npm install in tools/oracle)
